definition: Reducing words to base forms: stemming chops affixes crudely (fast, error-prone on Arabic), lemmatization maps to true dictionary lemmas using morphological analysis (accurate, heavier).
details: Reducing words to base forms: stemming chops affixes crudely (fast, error-prone on Arabic), lemmatization maps to true dictionary lemmas using morphological analysis (accurate, heavier). For Arabic search, light stemming plus normalization is the pragmatic classical baseline; embeddings shifted the burden but did not eliminate it.

explainer.lead: Stemming and lemmatization are two ways of reducing words to base forms. The choice matters because stemming is fast but crude, while lemmatization is accurate but heavier.

tiers.eli5: Both shrink words to a core form: one just chops off the endings, the other looks the word up and gives its proper dictionary form.
tiers.practitioner: Stemming chops affixes crudely and is fast but error-prone, notably on Arabic; lemmatization maps to true dictionary lemmas using morphological analysis, accurate but heavier. For Arabic search, light stemming plus normalization is the pragmatic classical baseline, and embeddings shifted the burden but did not eliminate it.
tiers.paperLevel: Stemming reduces inflected or derived words by affix removal; lemmatization maps to true dictionary lemmas using morphological analysis. The trade-off is speed and error rate against accuracy and cost.

explainer.example: For Arabic search, a system uses light stemming plus normalization as its baseline; embeddings are added but do not remove the need for that normalization.
